chunks: 21 – Nuqayʿ b. al-Ḥārith, Abū Dāwud, al-Sabīʿī, al-Hamdānī. Narrated from Abū Barza Naḍla b. Abī ʿAbdillāh al-Aslamī, and narrated from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him).
In his ḥadīth there is (material that is) not recognized, and what I regard (to be appropriate) is to halt with his ḥadīth. And it is permissible for him to be brought out as a witness.

key_terms.التَّوَقُّفُ: Holding in suspense or uncertainty regarding a narrator's reliability
key_terms.شَاهِدًا: As a supporting witness or corroborating evidence, rather than primary proof
key_terms.مَنَاكِرُ: Unrecognized or unusual narrations, often indicating weakness or irregularity

ai.seo_question: What is the status of Nuqayʿ ibn al-Harith in Shia hadith sciences?
ai.summary: This biographical entry discusses Nuqayʿ ibn al-Ḥārith, a narrator from the Saba'i tribe. The scholar notes that his narrations contain 'manakir' (unrecognized or unusual material), leading to a verdict of 'tawaqquf' (holding in suspense/uncertainty) regarding his reliability, though he is still permissible to cite as a supporting witness (shahid).
